Subject: Planned egress-router firmware rotation — ORD region (Apr 25–26)

Hi Samir / Acme ops team,

We are planning a staged firmware rotation for the egress routing layer in the ORD region to address a NIC firmware regression that can cause transient packet drops under sustained >10Gbps flows. The maintenance window we have tentatively proposed is Apr 25 00:00–06:00 CDT (Apr 25–26 overnight UTC), performed as a rolling rotation across the four ORD availability zones.

What to expect:
- Window per-AZ: ~15–30 minutes of active rotation; each AZ will be taken one at a time.
- Impact: short connection resets for affected TCP flows during the individual AZ rotation (typically 30–90s).
- Long-lived streams (websockets / HTTP/2): may require reconnects; we aim to keep overall API throughput within SLOs via multi-AZ failover.
- Dedicated customers: traffic pinned to a reserved rack will be moved off target racks temporarily during rotation; Dedicated tenants may see re-routing but no data plane access loss beyond reconnection windows.

Mitigations we will apply:
- Staggered AZ rotation with health checks and automated rollback.
- Active traffic draining and session migration where supported.
- Prefix/KV cache persistence; model in-memory caches are preserved across the router rotation.
- Increased retry/backoff guidance published in the runbook (attached).

Attachments: ORD_egress_router_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook, steps & rollback), impact_matrix_ORD_Apr25.xlsx (customer-specific impact matrix).

If this window conflicts with your low-traffic periods, let us know preferred 2-hour window overnight CDT and we can try to accommodate. Also tell us if any of your production flows rely on sticky long-lived TCP sessions that cannot be re-established automatically.

Escalation contact during the window: +1-555-0129 (On-call infrastructure).

Thanks,
Rachel

Hi Samir — quick technical notes from infra: \n
- For long-lived streams: affected flows will experience a TCP teardown during the brief interface re-initialization on the router. In practice we see client-side reconnects within 30–90s for gRPC/websocket flows; application-level state (model sessions) is preserved at the service tier.
- Transparent failover is limited by client behavior; if your clients do not implement exponential backoff + reconnect, they may need a small change. We can provide a short snippet for recommended client reconnect logic.
- If we detect an anomaly during a rotation, automated rollback takes ~5–10 minutes; full traffic restoration to prior routing patterns is typically complete within 10–20 minutes after rollback completes.
- We will perform a canary on a non-critical AZ first then proceed sequentially; manual holdpoints between AZs.

I attached the impact matrix so you can see which flows map to the affected egress paths. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through specifics — propose Mon Apr 21 09:00 CDT if that works.

—Marcus
